paper_summary: Archaeological conservation study of a Late Period Egyptian polychrome wooden coffin from Dahshur: the object was characterised by optical/stereo/digital microscopy, 2D and photogrammetric 3D documentation, SEM-EDX, XRD and wood anatomy (yellow layer = goethite/yellow ochre, ground layer = calcite plus gypsum, textile = linen plain weave, wood = Ficus sycomorus and Quercus cerris). Conservation comprised mechanical and chemical cleaning (xylene/distilled water 1:1 on the black resin layer, ethyl alcohol/water on the painted layer), reassembly with beech dowels and Paraloid B72 (15 % and 50 %), gap filling with cotton and with glass microballoons in Paraloid B72 (15 %), and consolidation of the painted layer with nano-silica in Klucel G (0.5 %). No hollow-particle composite was fabricated or mechanically characterised.
extraction_notes: Off-topic for the syntactic-foam database. The only hollow-particle material mentioned is a commercial 'glass microballoon' filler paste mixed with Paraloid B72 (15 % in acetone) that was used to level losses and cracks in the coffin before retouching ('After complete drying, a glass microballoon was used in paraloid B72 (15%) to level the surface and prepare for the colouring process of the completed parts', Loss Compensation section; Figs. 19, 21, 22). No microballoon grade, size, density, volume or weight fraction is given, and the paper reports no mechanical, thermal or physical property measurement of that filler or of any composite - a keyword sweep of the whole file finds no MPa/GPa, modulus, strength, density or fraction values anywhere. All quantitative numbers in the paper concern the object (190 x 51 x 55 cm coffin, 15 cm dowel), instrument settings (SEM 30 kV; XRD 40 kV / 30 mA), wood anatomy (vessel lumina 100-200 um and >200 um) and reagent concentrations (Paraloid B72 15 % / 50 %, Klucel G 1 % and 0.5 %, nano-silica in Klucel G 0.5 %). Therefore is_syntactic_foam_paper=false and records=[] per rule 6/10.
